findings.message:
Unrequested change to the ping call may break every ping.

The call moves from `SendPingAsync(ipAddress, _options.TimeoutMilliseconds)` to a named-argument overload with a `TimeSpan`, `buffer: null`, `options: null`, and a `CancellationToken`. The PR description does not mention this change. Two risks:
- The overload's signature is unverified. If `timeout` isn't a `TimeSpan` or `buffer` isn't nullable, the build fails.
- I believe `Ping` has historically rejected a null `buffer` with `ArgumentNullException` (unverified). If so, every ping hits the generic catch at line 184, logs a warning, and every device is reported offline.

The existing tests would not catch this. `CheckAllDevicesAsync_DoesNotUpdateDevice_WhenStatusUnchanged` ([test/API/DeviceMonitoringServiceTests.cs:256](https://github.com/renedierking/LANdalf/blob/bc1698f4dbc3a99dee0a6dcf7629813f2027682a/test/API/DeviceMonitoringServiceTests.cs#L256)) expects no update for an unreachable IP. `CheckAllDevicesAsync_PingsDevicesWithIpAddress` (line 222) asserts `Times.AtMostOnce`. Both pass whether or not pings work.

**Fix:** Revert to the original `SendPingAsync(ipAddress, _options.TimeoutMilliseconds)`. If cancellation is needed, add it with an explicit non-null buffer and confirm the overload by building.

Shutdown cancellation is reported as a failed ping.

Once the token reaches `SendPingAsync`, a host shutdown during a ping throws `OperationCanceledException`. That is neither a `PingException` nor a `PlatformNotSupportedException`, so the generic catch logs "Unexpected error pinging" at Warning and returns `false`. `CheckDeviceAsync` then sets `IsOnline = false`, clears `OnlineSince`, and calls `UpdatePcDeviceAsync` with the cancelled token (line 143). `SaveChangesAsync` honors the token, so the write most likely aborts. The warning still fires for every in-flight device on every shutdown.

**Fix:** Add `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) { throw; }` before the generic catch, or revert the token as in item 1.

`iputils-ping` does not affect .NET's `Ping`, so the guidance points at the wrong fix.

- The app uses only `System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping`, and nothing in `src/` launches a `ping` process. On Linux, .NET's `Ping` opens ICMP sockets in-process (from my knowledge of the runtime), so the installed binary never runs. The PR's goal of making "ICMP ping commands work inside the container" assumes it does.
- The app runs as `appuser` after `exec gosu appuser` ([`src/API/docker-entrypoint.sh:10`](https://github.com/renedierking/LANdalf/blob/bc1698f4dbc3a99dee0a6dcf7629813f2027682a/src/API/docker-entrypoint.sh#L10)), which has no `CAP_NET_RAW`. Unprivileged ICMP needs the `net.ipv4.ping_group_range` sysctl to include the process's group. `docker-compose.yaml` uses `network_mode: host`, so that sysctl comes from the host, not the image.
- Debian's `ping` carries the `cap_net_raw` file capability (packaging knowledge, unverified here). The package therefore adds a raw-socket-capable binary that the app never calls.

**Fix:** Remove `iputils-ping` unless code will invoke `/usr/bin/ping`. If ICMP is required, grant `NET_RAW` to the app process or set `ping_group_range` on the host, then rewrite the log text and Dockerfile comment to match. Verify with `docker compose up --build` that a device ping succeeds.

Environment guidance is logged only at Debug.

The remediation text is emitted per failing device per cycle at Debug, so it is invisible at the default `Information` level. Permission failures are otherwise silent, and every device just shows offline. **Fix:** Log the address at Debug, and emit one Warning behind the existing `Interlocked` guard with guidance that matches what the image provides.
